2609.02796.title: DiscoSign: Discourse-Aware Text to Sign Language Gloss Translation
2609.02796.paper_summary: Sign language processing systems have traditionally operated at the sentence level, ignoring critical discourse phenomena fundamental to sign language comprehension. We introduce DiscoSign, a computational approach for discourse-aware text to sign language gloss translation grounded in linguistic research. We address three key phenomena within our modular Large Language Model (LLM)-based translation framework: (i) spatial coreference resolution, where entities maintain consistent spatial locations throughout discourse; (ii) Question-Answer Clauses (QACs), pseudocleft structures serving specific discourse functions; and (iii) concept-gloss consistency, ensuring stable mappings between English concepts and American Sign Language (ASL) signs. Traditional translation metrics fail to capture discourse-level quality, so we introduce a suite of novel evaluation metrics designed to assess each dimension of discourse coherence addressed by our framework. Experiments on sentence-level and discourse-level datasets show that our approach for discourse-aware processing significantly improves spatial consistency and entity tracking relative to sentence-only translation, while maintaining competitive single-sentence gloss translation quality. Our work establishes the first systematic framework for discourse-level text to sign language gloss translation with corresponding evaluation methodology.
2609.02796.paper_summary_zh: 手語處理系統傳統上在句子層面運作，忽略了對手語理解至關重要的關鍵話語現象。我們介紹了 DiscoSign，一種基於語言研究的話語感知文本到手語詞彙翻譯的計算方法。我們在模塊化的大型語言模型 (LLM) 基礎翻譯框架中處理三個關鍵現象：(i) 空間共指解析，其中實體在整個話語中保持一致的空間位置；(ii) 問題-回答子句 (QACs)，用於特定話語功能的偽切分結構；以及 (iii) 概念-詞彙一致性，確保英語概念與美國手語 (ASL) 手勢之間的穩定映射。傳統翻譯指標未能捕捉話語層面的質量，因此我們引入了一套新穎的評估指標，旨在評估我們框架所處理的每個話語連貫性維度。在句子層面和話語層面的數據集上的實驗顯示，我們的話語感知處理方法相較於僅句子翻譯顯著改善了空間一致性和實體跟蹤，同時保持了具有競爭力的單句詞彙翻譯質量。我們的工作建立了第一個系統化的話語層面文本到手語詞彙翻譯框架，並附有相應的評估方法。
